Being deeply embedded in a community, especially one with strong shared beliefs and values like a church, can indeed have both positive and negative effects on your ability to think for yourself. On the one hand, being part of a close-knit community can provide a sense of belonging, support, and guidance. It can be comforting to be surrounded by like-minded individuals who share your values and beliefs. This can be especially true when it comes to navigating complex moral or ethical issues, as you can draw on the collective wisdom and experiences of your community. On the other hand, being too deeply ingrained in a single community can potentially limit your exposure to diverse perspectives, ideas, and ways of thinking. When you're surrounded by people who largely share the same views, you may not be challenged to question or critically evaluate your own beliefs as often. This can lead to a kind of "groupthink" or echo chamber effect, where you may unintentionally adopt the opinions and values of those around you without fully considering alternative viewpoints. Additionally, the pressure to conform to the norms and expectations of your community can be strong, especially if you're deeply invested in the relationships and social bonds within that community. This can make it more difficult to speak out or think differently, even if you have doubts or reservations about certain issues. This can help you develop a more nuanced and open-minded approach to thinking about complex issues. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?
